summary: Wild Horse fire lookout on Lakit Mountain, established 1955; decommissioned 1976 and replaced by a 1977 replica shelter open to hikers.

facts.design: Replacement shelter built to the original lookout design in 1977
facts.status_note: The fire lookout was decommissioned in 1976. The 1977 building on the site is a replacement shelter that matches the original design.

staffing.status: Manned for fire service when first erected (blog account)

access.note: Maintained recreation site, free to access. The lookout is reached by a hike from a trailhead at the end of a rough road.

visit.trail_note: About 2.3 km one way from the trailhead, with about 480 m of climb. The road to the trailhead is about 7.4 km (Cranbrook page) or 7.5 km (trail page), and the trail page recommends a high clearance vehicle.

events.note: Established as the Wild Horse Lookout.
Erected and manned for service from the start, according to a blog account.
Decommissioned as a fire lookout in 1976, per the trail page. The Cranbrook page says it served until the mid-1970s and that the original was then removed.
Replacement shelter built to match the original design, open to hikers and backcountry users. A blog calls it a replica.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Cranbrook page says the lookout served until the mid-1970s. The trail page says it was an active part of the provincial fire suppression program for about a dozen years, yet also dates its decommissioning to 1976. The story reports both accounts and does not choose between them.
The blog calls the fire lookout abandoned. The Cranbrook page calls the site a maintained shelter. Both fit a building that no longer watches for fires but is kept open to visitors.

notes_for_editor: Three independent-looking sources agree on the 1955 Wild Horse start and the 1977 replacement shelter. They disagree on the years in service (see resolved_conflicts). The official Sites and Trails BC page (sitesandtrailsbc.ca/resource/REC2366) returned no text to fetch, so it is not cited, although search snippets show it names the lookout as 2354 m. The Cranbrook page gives 2,346 m. The story does not give an elevation. The brief agency Recreation Sites and Trails BC is supported by the trail page title. The brief status unknown is replaced by replica. The steveamie blog is the only source for manned for service and for the woodstove and bed. The Life is Adventure blog's replica wording conflicts with nothing else, but it is a blog, so it is used only for those points.
